note: MADE-UP sample for the tests and the demo: one stage in the compact single-stage form of the curriculum files (CURRICULUM_FORMAT.md §3). stage holds the stage's own fields; the top level holds its skills, greetingActivityIds, topics, lessonTemplates and trackerRows beside activities, equipment and safety. Every name and sentence is invented; none of it is YMCA text.

activities.name: Otter Bubbles
activities.description: Everyone joins the otter crew: take one breath, put your face in, blow bubbles for a count of three, then come up and wave.

activities.name: Beaver Peekaboo
activities.description: Swimmers hum like a beaver while blowing bubbles, first on the surface, then with mouth and nose under the water. Bring a watering can or a bucket.

activities.name: Tugboat Treasure Hunt
activities.description: A helper points to a spot on the bottom near the steps. Swimmers take one breath, look under at it, and come back up to say what they saw. Bring a hoop or a floating mat.

safety.text: One breath at a time: swimmers take a single normal breath before each time they go under, never several deep breaths in a row.

topics.name: Meeting the Group
topics.summary: Talk about meeting the group and what it looks like at the pool.
prompts: What is one thing you want to try today?
Who can you ask for help at the pool?

topics.name: Pool Rules
topics.summary: Share one idea about pool rules and try it during the lesson.
prompts: Why do we walk instead of run on the deck?
What does a good listener do?

topics.name: Asking First
topics.summary: Swimmers name one way to practise asking first today.
prompts: How can you help a friend who feels nervous?
What makes you feel safe in the water?

topics.name: Sun and Water
topics.summary: Talk about sun and water and what it looks like at the pool.
prompts: What did you do well today?

topics.name: Being Kind
topics.summary: Share one idea about being kind and try it during the lesson.
prompts: What would you like to practise next time?
Where is a safe place to wait for your turn?

topics.name: Trying New Things
topics.summary: Swimmers name one way to practise trying new things today.
prompts: What can you do if you get tired in the water?
How do you know when it is your turn?

topics.name: Helping Out
topics.summary: Talk about helping out and what it looks like at the pool.
prompts: What is your favourite pool game, and why?
Who watches you when you are near water?

topics.name: Celebrating Progress
topics.summary: Share one idea about celebrating progress and try it during the lesson.
prompts: What should you do before getting in?
How does your body feel after swimming?
